entities.summary:
George Montagu, 4th Duke of Manchester PC, was a British politician and diplomat who served as the British Ambassador to Russia from 1775 to 1783. His tenure was marked by the negotiations with Catherine the Great, which led to the signing of the Treaty of London, a significant agreement between Great Britain and Russia that shaped the balance of power in Europe during the late 18th century. Montagu's diplomatic efforts also contributed to the establishment of the British-Russian Alliance, which played a crucial role in the War of the Austrian Succession. As a politician, Montagu was a strong advocate for the rights of the British people, particularly the working class, and was a key figure in the development of the British Factory Act of 1799. His legacy as a diplomat and statesman has endured, with many historians considering him one of the most influential British diplomats of his time.

Montagu was born around 1725, the son of the 3rd Duke of Manchester, and was educated at Eton and Trinity College, Cambridge. He entered politics at a young age, serving as a member of Parliament for the constituency of Manchester from 1754 to 1760. In 1765, he was raised to the peerage as Viscount Newhaven, and in 1776, he became the 4th Duke of Manchester.

Montagu's personal life was marked by controversy, particularly his involvement in the scandalous affair with Madame du Deffand, a French courtesan. The affair, which began in the 1760s, was widely publicized and caused significant damage to Montagu's reputation. Despite this, he remained a prominent figure in British society, known for his intelligence, wit, and charismatic personality.

In his later years, Montagu became increasingly involved in the affairs of the British Empire, serving as a member of the Privy Council and as a trustee of the East India Company. He died on September 2, 1788, at the age of 63, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most influential British politicians of his time.
